So basically replacing tools like Cursor/Conductor/Traycer with just a set of skills. Our hope is that the entire AI harness eventually becomes open source and modular. 15 16 ## Quickstart 17 18 Install OpenAgent, on macOS or Linux: 19 20 ```bash 21 npx @openagt/install 22 ``` 23 24 From then on, https://openagent.build opens your dashboard, on this computer. It starts when you log in, and `openagent` runs the same copy in a terminal. `openagent --uninstall` takes it off again. 25 26 Or try it once, with nothing installed, in your project's folder: 27 28 ```bash 29 npx @openagt/dashboard 30 ``` 31 32 It opens the dashboard in your browser, on your project. Every agent you start gets the skills of OpenAgent's core modules (github's on a GitHub project) and of the plugins on in your project, with nothing written in your project; a skill of your own with the same name takes one's place. Each plugin is switched on or off in Settings › Plugins: ask and desktop notifications start on, the others (the tickets, the queue, the logs, the browser, the scheduler…) start off. 33 34 A project's own skills are files in it, which the dashboard lists in Settings › Skills; the Skills line in the gear's menu under the message box picks the ones a run gets, and the plugins it goes without. A plugin's skills come with it, in its package, and reach OpenAgent's runs only: the tickets with the commands about them, the queue with work-queue, the logs, and the others.
